svg.title: sort -S 100b on eight lines: three sorted runs written to files, then merged through a heap

g.title: Each line costs its bytes, a NUL, and 24 bytes of header and pointer. 3 lines are held, 91 bytes; the next, "she", would make 119, past the 100 that -S allows. So the 3 are sorted, written out as run 1, and let go.
3 lines are held, 86 bytes; the next, "the", would make 114, past the 100 that -S allows. So the 3 are sorted, written out as run 2, and let go.
The input ends with 2 lines held, 58 bytes: they are sorted and written as run 3. No more than 100 bytes of lines were ever in memory at once.
The merge opens the three runs and pushes each into a heap, ordered by its first line: run 2, whose next line is "always", is on top.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 2 has the smallest next line, "always", and it is written out. Its next line, "is", puts run 2 back in the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 1 has the smallest next line, "holmes", and it is written out. Its next line, "sherlock", puts run 1 back in the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 2 has the smallest next line, "is", and it is written out. Its next line, "she", puts run 2 back in the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 2 has the smallest next line, "she", and it is written out. Run 2 is used up and leaves the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 1 has the smallest next line, "sherlock", and it is written out. Its next line, "to", puts run 1 back in the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 3 has the smallest next line, "the", and it is written out. Its next line, "woman", puts run 3 back in the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: run 1 has the smallest next line, "to", and it is written out. Run 1 is used up and leaves the heap.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line

g.title: Pop: "woman", the last line, from run 3. Every run is used up: the output is the eight lines in order, the same bytes as sort without -S.
g.text: the heap: one entry per run, by its next line
